output.murderer: Dr Casimir Vauthier, the family physician
output.reasoning:
Fixing the clocks first, using the testimony that agrees with itself:
- Rosa's kitchen clock runs 15 minutes fast. Casimir's watch ran 2 minutes fast at dinner. Together they give piano start at 10:43 true and piano stop at 10:56 true. Casimir's own times (out at 10:45 by his watch, back shortly before the hall struck eleven) match this.
- Girard's watch runs 14 minutes slow: his piano cue at 10:29 is 10:43 true. So his 10:34 bells are 10:48 true, and his return at 10:46 is 11:00 true.
- The hall clock was 2 minutes fast at 10:58 true (Rosa and Girard agree). It was 12 minutes fast when it struck ten at 9:48 true (Lina). Someone set it back about 10 minutes between those hours, which is the murderer's hand.
- Félix's watch runs slow. Girard reached the library at about 11:00–11:02 true, which Félix logged as 10:32. That puts his offset at about 30 minutes. His thump at 10:18 is then 10:48 true, matching Girard's bells. His stair traffic (up at 10:15, down at 10:21) is 10:45 and 10:51 true.

Alibis: Odile was at the piano from 10:43 to 10:56, heard by Rosa and Girard. Rosa and Lina were in the kitchen together from about 10:32 to 11:00, each vouching for the other. Girard was outside under the front windows. Félix was in the library, with no one vouching for him. Casimir was in the hall from 10:43 to 10:56 and gave no account of the roughly ten minutes beyond fetching his cigar case. The hall and the stairs lie between him and the atelier.

The regulator is the decisive clue. It reads 10:05, but Lina says it was running at 10:20 when the master was alive, so the 10:05 reading was set afterwards by someone in the atelier between about 10:20 and the murder. A stopped time of 10:05 is alibied only by the piquet game, in which Casimir and Odile were together at the table. That is precisely the time someone would fake to clear himself. The same visit fits the stair traffic and the hall clock adjustment.

Félix had no reason to be in the hall. Girard was outside with an unverifiable but consistent account. Casimir is the only candidate whose story hides an unexplained stretch and whose hall-and-stairs route fits all the disturbances. The repeater's ten low notes, some doubled quarter notes and quick high minutes agree with 10:48.
